game_note: Boiling point of water is only 100 C at sea level on Earth: exposed equipment must survive worse.
Night lasts about 14.8 Earth days: batteries and heaters must bridge it.
Largest day-night temperature swing of any body commonly visited - thermal design is a core trade-off in this game.
source_name: Derived from NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet day/night values

game_note: Cold on average, yet hot at noon: the average hides the extremes.
Some polar crater floors never receive direct sunlight - the coldest measured places in the solar system.
source_name: NASA SSERVI - LRO Finds Coldest Place on the Moon

game_note: About 100 m down, shadows stay near room temperature all lunar day: pits are natural shelters.
source_name: NASA - LRO Finds Lunar Pits Harbor Comfortable Temperatures

game_note: The day/night heat wave barely reaches one metre down: subsurface temperature is stable.
source_name: Derived from LRO pit temperature studies

game_note: Loose regolith is an excellent insulator: the surface swings ~295 K while a metre below barely changes.
